wave.summary: Built server/gitFacts.js: plain-Node ESM async gitFacts(repoPath) that shells out to git exclusively via execFile argv arrays and never throws. Returns the git-derived RepoSummary fields per the frozen shared/contract.js: name/path/id (kebab slug), branch or detached short-sha, porcelain dirty, three-state upstream ({state:'tracked',aheadBy,behindBy}|{state:'none'}) via rev-list --left-right --count @{u}...HEAD with LEFT=behind/RIGHT=ahead parse order pinned by an asymmetric behind-only fixture (behindBy=2, aheadBy=0), commitDays from a 12-month %aI log bucketed with shared dayKey (TZ pinned America/Chicago), lastCommit, recentCommits (15, hash/iso/subject/author), touchedFiles (10 distinct paths from a name-only log with lastIso+commit counts), and branches (current first, then tip-date desc). Hostile inputs — empty zero-commit repo, .git-file worktree (verified .git is a file), detached HEAD, no-upstream branch, non-repo dir, nonexistent path — all resolve to usable partials with upstream {state:'none'}, never a zero ahead-count and never a throw. Tests build real throwaway repos in a mktemp root (init -b, commits with explicit --date + GIT_AUTHOR_DATE/GIT_COMMITTER_DATE literals, isolated GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL/SYSTEM, worktree add for the .git-file case, a local origin + three clones for behind-only/ahead-only/diverged/in-sync), no network, no Date.now in assertions. Committed as 5cef937 on the worktree branch; only in-scope files staged.

wave.summary: Built the attention engine in server/attention.js (plain Node ESM) on top of the frozen shared contract: classify(repo, nowIso) returns {reasons, displayState} where reasons is every applicable AttentionReason filtered through ATTENTION_ORDER (so a repo can be dirty AND stale) and displayState is the strongest reason, falling back to 'no-remote' for upstream {state:'none'} and 'ok' otherwise; unpushed requires upstream.state==='tracked' && aheadBy>0, so a no-remote repo can never be unpushed; staleness delegates to contract isStale (strict >90 days). buildAttention(repos, nowIso) emits one AttentionEntry per attention-needing repo (strongest reason, lastActivityIso = lastCommit.iso) and returns it pre-sorted via contract sortAttention — no comparator logic duplicated. TDD: wrote server/attention.test.js first (confirmed red, then green) covering every displayState, tracked-behind not-unpushed, the exact boundary (90d = not stale, 90d+1s = stale against fixed nowIso 2026-08-01T12:00:00Z), all multi-reason combos, no-remote-never-unpushed under every combination, band ordering dirty>unpushed>stale with recency-desc tie-breaks and stable order on identical instants, exclusion of ok/no-remote repos, and exact reproduction of the canonical shared fixture attention queue. node_modules was already present in the worktree (tracked in this repo), so no symlink was needed. wave.summary:
Built the four hand-rolled SVG chart components, bare props-in/SVG-out (no Plate wrapper, no chart libraries), using only tokens.css vars and the shared/contract.js render vocabulary.

Heatmap {commitDays, endDayKey, onDayClick}: 53-column x 7-row GitHub-style grid (Sun..Sat rows), anchored at endDayKey's week. Every one of the 371 cells always renders (no truncation), level = 0 for zero commits else min(count,4), rendered via heatmapLevelClass(). Month labels placed at each column whose Sunday starts a new calendar month. Each cell is a rect with data-daykey, role=button, tabIndex=0, and both click and Enter/Space call onDayClick(dayKey) — the cross-filter emit.

Timeline {commitDays, filterDay?}: derives its own 52-week trailing window from the max key present in commitDays (no endDayKey prop), draws an impulse+area "sounding" (vertical stems + dot markers + a faint area under the curve). When filterDay falls inside the window, the containing week gets a `--active` modifier (full ink, larger dot), every other week gets `--dim` (28% opacity), a dashed marker line is drawn at the exact day position within that week, and a mono tabular-figure reading (.sounding) shows the date and that week's count — this is the tested, visibly-different render. An out-of-window filterDay is a documented no-op (no crash, nothing marked).

Sparkline {series}: generic numeric-series sounding line with an end-value reading; safe on 0-length and 1-length series.

Strata {loc}: horizontal LOC bar split into per-language bands using the frozen `.strata-band` class (sepia fill) with a hatch-pattern overlay (angle/spacing cycled per band, stroked in var(--ink)) so languages are told apart by texture, never hue — respecting the "vermilion is attention-only" and "no ad-hoc colors" rules. A legend below lists each language with its LOC in mono tabular figures (.sounding, via toLocaleString). Safe on empty loc (renders a single faint placeholder band).

charts.test.tsx (16 tests): Heatmap/Timeline expected values (window bounds, anchor weekday, per-level cell histogram, month-label columns, week totals) are hand-derived from the canonical fixture Snapshot with the derivation spelled out in comments — computed independently of the components' internals, not by re-running their logic. Verified two of these tests are load-bearing via mutation probes (broke the level-cap and the dim-class assignment; both correctly turned tests red, then green again on restore). Every chart also has an explicit empty-data render test asserting no throw.

npm test: 53/53 green (37 pre-existing contract tests + 16 new chart tests). node_modules was already present/tracked in the worktree (git worktree add checked it out since it's tracked in this repo, no symlink needed); I reverted the incidental vitest results.json cache diff after each run so only my 6 in-scope files are part of the commit.
